text:
alex: Quick sync — we need an ordered cutover playlist for tenant residency moves (active -> active handoff) that avoids double-writes and respects data-residency flags. Proposed high-level steps below, want flags/edge cases.

sam: +1. Do we assume control-plane atomic commit for leases or do we need two-phase commit? :thinking:

jordan: I sketched a minimal, conservative sequence:
```
1) mark tenant: state=pre-cutover, reason=operator
2) start drain on old-primary (stop new writes at proxy)
3) prewarm caches & indices in target region
4) swap lease on control-plane (single API call)
5) switch proxy routing header -> X-Region-Hint: <target>
6) accept writes in target; run fast reconciliation job for 30s
7) clear drain & mark cutover complete
```
This avoids concurrent write windows if proxies honor drain.

maria: Important: for EU-residency customers we must not forward nonconsenting writes out of-region during step 6. Either block or escrow. @alex we should gate by tenant.policy.residency_allow_forwarding.

ken: Ops note — need throttles during step 6. If traffic spikes the reconciliation job will fall behind and we could surface duplicate events to downstream. Suggest a short write-rate cap (10rps -> ramp) + observability. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

alex: Good call. Add explicit throttles and a reconciliation window. Also we need a safe fallback if KV sync lag > threshold (e.g., >500ms p99 or >count of outstanding ops >1000). Fallback = rollback routing + re-drain old-primary.

sam: How do proxies detect the cutover boundary? Options: control-plane route (push) vs client-hint header injection. I prefer control-plane push so clients don't need changes. But push increases blast radius.

jordan: Control-plane push + proxy local cache works. Sequence for push: set proxy route state -> write-block -> client reconnects -> new route applied. Edge: long-lived connections (websockets) need per-connection handshake to pick up new region.

maria: Legal/regulatory question: For tenants with residency hard-lock, step 4 must include an assert that target region is allowed. If assert fails we must escalate and abort. Add a pre-check: tenant.policy.allowed_regions contains target.

ken: Ops-runbook snippet suggestion (to paste into runbook):
```
# ordered-cutover quick run
1) PRECHECK: verify policy + capacity in target
2) FLAG: set tenant.state=pre-cutover
3) DRAIN: proxy -> stop writes (keep reads)
4) PREWARM: cache, KV warm, model weights if needed
5) LEASE_SWAP: commit lease to target (control-plane)
6) REROUTE: push route to proxies + clients
7) MONITOR: check error-rate, p99 latency, kv-lag metric
8) FINALIZE: unset draining flags
```

alex: For automation, we need idempotent APIs: `POST /tenants/:id/cutover` should be safe to retry and report intermediate state. Also add `?dry_run=true`.

sam: Reconciliation job details: use per-tenant sequence number and convert conflicting writes into merge-conflict events that are processed by offline job. Avoid user-visible duplicates by deduping on sequence id.

jordan: We should also add a fast-path for low-risk tenants: if tenant has 0 writes in last 5m, we can do immediate lease-swap with a 10s drain and skip heavy prewarm. Label it `expedite=true` but require operator override.

maria: For audit/compliance include an immutable cutover record (who triggered, timestamps, precheck results) and wire that into the tenant's audit log. :ledger:

ops-bot: Canary cutover automation run queued for tenant=acme-corp region=eu-west-1; id=run-20260301-42

ken: One more: telemetry. Emit events for every step (precheck_ok, drained, lease_swap_ok, routed, reconcile_ok). These allow us to build a live cutover dashboard and automated rollback conditions.

alex: OK next steps: jordan to turn sequence into a durable state-machine RFC; sam to write reconcile plan; maria to enumerate residency policy asserts; ken to draft runbook + alert thresholds. I'll own the automation API shape.

sam: noted. I'll start a small sim to prove the dedupe strategy.

jordan: I'll draft the RFC this week, include sequence diagram and failure scenarios.

maria: I'll collate legal edgecases and share a short checklist.

alex: Thanks everyone. If you spot a missing failure mode call it out here or DM. :thumbsup:
